preconditions.description: The number of nodes in the tree s is between 2 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes in the range 1 to n.
The input describes a tree with exactly n-1 edges.

postconditions.description: The number of nodes in the T-decomposition is between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(len(xi) >= 1 and all(1 <= node <= n for node in xi) for xi in decomposition_nodes)
postconditions.description: Each node in the T-decomposition contains at least one node from the original tree s, and all nodes in xi are within the valid range.
The union of all nodes in the T-decomposition equals the set of all nodes in the original tree s.

postconditions.expression: all(any(a in xi and b in xi for xi in decomposition_nodes) for a, b in edges)
postconditions.description: For every edge (a, b) in the original tree s, there exists at least one node in the T-decomposition that contains both a and b.

postconditions.expression: all(any(a in xi for xi in path) for a in set(range(1, n + 1)) for xi, xj in decomposition_edges if a in xi and a in xj for path in all_paths_between(xi, xj, decomposition_edges))
postconditions.description: For any two nodes xi and xj in the T-decomposition that both contain a node a from the original tree s, all nodes in the T-decomposition lying on the path between xi and xj also contain a.

postconditions.expression: max(len(xi) for xi in decomposition_nodes) == min_weight
postconditions.description: The weight of the T-decomposition (maximum cardinality of any node) is minimized.
The number of nodes in the T-decomposition is the smallest possible among all optimal T-decompositions.
